newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli settlements recipe for confrontation - PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israeli settlements recipe for confrontation - PLO.

text.p: An Israeli expansion of Jewish settlements on occupied Arab land will trigger clashes between Israel and the Palestinians, a PLO official said on Sunday.
"If Israel continues to confiscate Arab land to expand settlements for Jews on Palestinian land, then it is asking for confrontations," said Palestinian Public Works Minister Azzam al-Ahmad.

"The Palestinian Authority will not allow Israel to swallow Palestinian land. This is a decision, and if clashes over settlements occur, Netanyahu's government will be fully responsible for triggering such clashes," al-Ahmad told Reuters.

PLO officials use words such as "cancerous" to describe settlements. President Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority on Friday formed committees to battle a renewed settlements policy under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Palestinians have been killed in clashes with Israeli soldiers and settlers over confiscation of Arab land to build roads and settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Some 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered among the more than two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.

"The expansion of Jewish settlements on Palestinian land is an issue that will lead to confrontation between Israelis and Palestinian because settlements are illegal, are colonisation and apartheid," Azmi Bishara, an Arab member of Israel's parliament said in a seminar in Ramallah.

Under the 1993 PLO-Israel peace deal, Israel has handed over parts of the West Bank and Gaza to Palestinian self-rule but the fate of settlements has been left to "final-status" talks that have yet to resume since Netanyahu took office in June.

Arafat said on Sunday the expansion of settlements was a breach of the peace deal stating that each side would refrain from taking unilateral steps that would prejudice the outcome of talks on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza.
Netanyahu enraged Palestinians when he lifted a four-year freeze on Jewish settlement construction after he took office.

He has approved the construction of thousands of new homes for Jews in the West Bank since August. But, much to the chagrin of settler groups that helped bring him to power, he has not gone ahead with plans for new settlements.
